summary.en: Ethiopian-linked drones struck near Khartoum, killing four and damaging a United Nations building, while infantry fighting was reported along the Ethiopia-Eritrea border in Gemalo locality. The UK has expanded its travel advisory to include Arsi and East Borena zones, and clashes in Moyale have entered a sixth week, driving displacement despite peace talks. Tensions persist as the Sudanese capital rejected Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's peace bid and a RSF-linked delegation visited Addis Ababa, while aid workers report both protection in Somalia and obstruction at home. The conflict has produced 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Etiopia-tilknyttede droner traffet i nærheten av Khartoum, drepte fire og skadet en bygning til FN, mens infanterikamp ble rapportert langs grensen mot Eritrea i lokalsamfunnet Gemalo. Storbritannia har utvidet reiserådet til å omfatte Arsi‑ og Øst-Borena-sonene, og kampene i Moyale har nådd en sjette uke, noe som driver frem fordrivelse til tross for fredssamtaler. Spenningene vedvarer ettersom hovedstaden i Sudan avviste statsminister Abiy Ahmeds fredsinitiativ og en delegasjon knyttet til RSF-militsen besøkte Addis Ababa, mens hjelpearbeidere rapporterer både beskyttelse i Somalia og hindringer hjemme. Konflikten har forårsaket 2 824 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
